art_instructions: Show a clear transition from the sunlit school exterior to the cozy classroom interior at the open front door. The right side of the image features the whitewashed facade with Mediterranean blue wooden trim and a terracotta-tiled roof, a covered porch supported by two wooden columns, and a stone path leading up to the entrance. A low stone bird bath sits near the steps, and a bougainvillea vine climbs beside the blue-trimmed doorway; an olive tree and small herb planters complete the garden feel. Through the open door (hinged on the right, swung inward), the classroom is visible: a soft blue wall, a low honey-oak desk and chair, a colorful woven rug on the stone floor, and warm daylight from a large window. The Owl—mottled brown-and-cream feathers, round amber eyes, a green scarf at her neck, and a tiny satchel—appears mid-glide at the threshold, entering from left to right. Her wings are partly outstretched, feet extended as if about to touch down on the rug, beak slightly open in a cheerful hoot, eyes looking into the room. Size and placement: the Owl is foreground mid-size, about one quarter the height of the doorway, positioned slightly left of center with her body angled rightward so the action of entering is unmistakable. Lighting contrasts bright midday sun and crisp porch shadows outside with softer, bright natural light inside, making the doorway the visual divider. Keep shapes rounded, details clear, and the scene uncluttered for early readers.
